adrenaline increased the renal lithium elimination in intact rats and adrenalectomised rats, and that α-adrenergics are involved in this effect.
the effect of adrenaline on renal excretion of lithium was mediated through the α-adrengic receptors.
Adrenaline increased the urinary clearance and fractional excretion of Li in adrenalecto-mized rats, an effect that was mediated by α-adrenoceptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of adrenaline on the renal elimination of lithium in adrenectomized rats.
the role of α- as well as β-adrenergically mediated effects in the action and metabolism of adrenaline in the adrenalectomised rat.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system and the adrenal medulla in the regulation of renal lithium elimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of adrenaline on the urinary clearance of LiCl in adrenalectomiczed rats are not directly dependent on the effects of the catecholamine on sodium, potassium, and water excretion.
adrenaline, by acting via α-adrenergics, can stimulate the renal lithium elimination in rats.
the action of L-adrenalina on renal lithium elimination is mediated by α- and β-receptors.

adrenaline, by stimulating α-adrenergically mediated vasoconstriction, increases the filtration of lithium, and that this increase in filtration rate is responsible for the observed increase in the urinary clearance.
the action of α-adrenergics on renal lithium elimination might be mediated via the α1- and α2-adrenergic receptor subtypes.
the α-adrenergetic effect of adrenaline on renal elimination of lithium is mediated via a β-adrenergically dependent mechanism.

adrenaline, in adrenalectomy rats, can be a good therapeutic option to increase renal lithium clearance.
